lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen, point and say Audio track 18

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the correct image. Say practises first-step pronunciation, including clear stress and blending in compound nouns like glue stick and marker pen.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear pronunciation  of words and confident repetition.
“Oh no! I’ve lost my school bag! Where could it be? Can you help me find it?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B. Listen and circle Audio track 19

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students listen for specific words or details, then show understanding by clearly circling the correct picture or number.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling, and neat work in students’ books.
“I’ve looked everywhere but I can’t find it! Maybe someone saw something. Let’s listen carefully and circle the right picture to help me look in the right place.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.67 - A Look & number

details: Look and number consolidates understanding of word–image connections. Students read words and look at visuals,  then show understanding by clearly writing the correct number.
Look for observation skills when viewing the visual, accurate choices of words for word recognition and neat number writing in students’ books.
“If I can remember what was in my bag, it might help. Let’s look at the pictures and match the words so I can make a list of everything I usually carry.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - C. Ask and Answer Audio track 20

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for correct use of ‘What have you got?’ questions, clear sentence answers, and consistent reference to the objects in the picture.

“If I can’t find my bag, can I borrow some of the things I need? Maybe one of you has something I can  borrow for the lesson. Ask your friend, ‘What have you got?’ and let’s see what everyone has in their bags.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - D. Ask and Answer Audio track 21 10m]

details: Ask and answer provides the opportunity to use the target structure with personalised information.
Look for accurate use of ‘What have you got?’  and ‘I’ve got a…’ plus school material vocabulary, correct pronunciation and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“Oh! My teacher just told me my mum called — I left my bag at home this morning! Let’s ask each other about our real bags while I figure out what I can borrow today.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - Chant p47 Audio track 22

details: Read, listen and say provides the opportunity to use the target structure and vocabulary in a chant as well as practising reading and listening skills.
Look for accurate reading as well as good pronunciation  as students  follow the lyrics.
“Thanks for helping me today. Now I know exactly what I need. Let’s sing the chant and hold up our school things so I remember to bring my bag tomorrow.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Chant): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video Chant):
